newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot to pay hourly for Russian engines.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot to pay hourly for Russian engines.

text.p: Russian international carrier Aeroflot has agreed with engine maker PermMotors to pay by the hour for the PS-90A engines on its long-range Ilyushin-96-300 jets, a company spokeswoman said on Monday.

Instead of Aeroflot buying the engines outright and paying to have them serviced, the airline would only pay for the time the engines are in use and in good working order during the first 20,000 hours of their life, an Aeroflot statement said.
OAO Permskiye Motory would be responsible for any servicing or repair work during that period, the statement said.

"We agreed to reject the outdated former Soviet system when the airline paid for bad quality engines. Now the engine maker will pay for repair work to the PS-90A if it has technical problems for which the maker is responsible during the first 20,000 hours," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
Aeroflot now pays about $1.5 million a month for repairs to the PS-90A, she said. The airline operates 64 PS-90As out of the 170 produced by Perm Motors.
Perm Motors chief executive Sergei Sopov said in a statement each PS-90A was working for about 10.5 hours a day in November compared with 3.9 hours in the same month of last year.
In the case of engine failure engine Perm Motors would replace it at its own cost, he added.

Both companies declined to say how much money Aeroflot would pay for one hour's use of an engine. But Aeroflot said it would pay for slightly less than 100 percent of flying time in order to set up an "insurance fund" to pay for urgent engine repairs if they occurred abroad.
"This agreement has mutual benefit because Perm Motors will improve the engine quality and Aeroflot will get dependable engines," the statement said.
Currently, about 40 percent of Russian-made passenger and aircraft are powered by Perm Motors engines.

The Aeroflot spokeswoman also said the airline planned to sign a similar agreement with Voronezh aviation plant which produces Il-96-300 passenger aircraft. "It will be the same with aircraft and avionics servicing," she said.
